_readme: §6 manifest-freeze allowlist. Read by packages/core/scripts/extension-manifest-audit.js
(rules permissions-frozen, host-permissions-frozen, content-script-matches-frozen), which runs
in test/smoke/audits/extension-manifest-audit.smoke.js and therefore in `pnpm test:smoke` on
every CI run. Any drift in manifest.json's permissions, host_permissions, or content-script
matches away from the values pinned below fails the release build.
SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY. This file lives in the same repository as manifest.json, so a single
commit can edit both together. That means this gate stops an ACCIDENT (a permission added for
one purpose that silently widens another, a stray edit that nobody meant to ship), not a
determined compromise by someone who already has write access to this repo. Because of that
limit, the release checklist (docs/QA_Checklist.md, "Chrome Web Store release provenance"
section) additionally requires the release operator to read a human diff of manifest.json
against the previous release tag before every submission. This file cannot replace that step.
web_accessible_resources is deliberately NOT pinned here as a third copy of the match list.
Spec §3.5 requires all three lists (content-script matches, and both web_accessible_resources
match lists) to stay identical, so the audit enforces that as a RELATIONSHIP: every WAR entry's
matches array is checked against manifest.json's own content_scripts matches at audit time
(rule war-matches-match-content-script), not against a second frozen copy in this file. A
second copy would let the two go stale together without either check ever firing.
Changing any value below is a deliberate manifest-surface decision (spec §8 D-items), not a
routine edit. Change it in the same commit that changes manifest.json, and say why.
